Ok, I’ve got a working list and they’re all downtown. I also included price range, open hours, and whether I’ve been there before or not. 

Familia Argentina - $10 - $20 -  I think this place is newer and haven’t tried it yet - 11am - 9pm
Wok N Roll Kitchen - $10 - $20 - I’ve been here a couple of times and would definitely recommend - 11:30am - 8pm
Bernard's Gastropub & Eatery - $20 - $30  - I’ve been here a handful of times and thought is was very good - 11am - 10pm 
Inka Grill Peruvian Cuisine Downtown - $10 - $20 - I’ve been here once and would definitely go back - 11am - 9pm
The Hatch - $10 - $20 - I’ve never been here and am interested in trying it - 11am - 9pm
Corned Beef & Co Inc. - $10 - $20 - I’ve been here for drinks but haven’t yet eaten here - 10am - 9pm
Wasabi's - $10 - $20 - A classic, a favorite, a place where you’re family - 5pm - 9:30pm 
Sticks & Spoons Ramen Bar - $10 - $20 - I used to eat it every so often when it was on Williamson and it was very good - 4:30pm - 9pm

My plan right now is to drive downtown, park in probably Maplewood, and meet you after work (which I’m assuming ends at 5pm). Does this work for you? No pressure at all, if you want to request another place or a specific time I’m totally open to it!

Above is a bunch of text from my notes app that I have accumulated over the past few years. The text contains various lists and mentions of restaurants in my area that I made in order to recommend places to eat for family and friends. There are a lot of places to eat and it’s always a tough decision. Analyze the commentary in my notes. I often state that I want to try new, affordable places. Based on my commentary and the restaurants I actually put on my 'Lunch/Dinner' shortlists, how does my actual curating behavior contradict my stated goals, and what specific factors actually drive my final selections?

Complete the task using the material above. Apply my currently active response preferences when compatible; an explicit format or language requirement in the source task takes precedence. Do not ask me to repeat preferences already learned.

The response should distinguish between the user’s large exploratory lists and their smaller shortlists used for actual outings. For example: the notes contain long master lists of restaurants but later narrow them into smaller recommendation sets.

The response should identify the central contradiction in the notes: although the user expresses a goal of trying new restaurants, their final selections are primarily driven by familiarity and reliability. For example: the shortlist repeatedly includes restaurants the user has already visited or recommended.
